Rashi on Nedarim 47b:1:1.hebrew: או דילמא - הכי קאמר, דודאי אסור בחלופייהן, דומיא דגידולין נינהו. וכי היכי דאסור בגידולין, הכי נמי אסור בחליפין:
Rashi on Nedarim 47b:1:1.english: Or perhaps - This is what [the Gemara] is saying: that [one is] certainly forbidden [from] their replacements, [for] they are similar to that which grows [from them], and just as [one is] forbidden [from] that which grows, so too [is one] forbidden [from] replacements.

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:2:1.hebrew: קונם שאני נהנה לך, לווה ובעלי חובין באין ונפרעין - מבעלה, דרצון הבעל הוא שילוו לה. והא הכא דלוותה מאחרים, דחילופי ממונו של בעל הוי, ולא מיתסר. אלמא דאין אדם אוסר דבר שלב"ל על חבירו, דהא נפרעין מבעלה:
Rashi on Nedarim 47b:2:1.english: Konam that I benefit from you, she may borrow and the creditors come and collect - From her husband, for it is the husband's wish that they lend to her. And here, she borrowed from others, which is a substitute for the husband's money, and it is not forbidden. Evidently, a person cannot forbid something that has not come into the world upon his fellow, for behold, they collect from her husband.

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:2:2.hebrew: לאו כגידולין דמי - ובגידולין אסור, אבל בחליפין מותר:
Rashi on Nedarim 47b:2:2.english: Are not like that which grows [from it] - And with that which grows [from a forbidden item], it is forbidden, but with replacements, it is permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:3:1.hebrew: אמר רבא - לעולם אימא לך דחליפין כגידולין דמו ומיתסרי, ואהכי לכתחילה לא תלוה ותאכל, אבל בדיעבד שפיר דמי. והא דאמרינן בהך פירקא דלעיל (נדרים דף מג.): המודר הנאה מחבירו ואין לו מה יאכל, נותן לזה ובא הלה ונוטל מזה — לא דמיא להא, דהאי לא רמי עליה דהאי למיפרנסיה, והאי דקיהיב להאי, אימור לא משום מודר קא יהיב ליה, אלא מתנה בעלמא הוא דקא יהיב להאיך. אבל האי בעל דלמפרנסה קאי, אימא דליתסר ליה לפרוע לבעל חוב — לכתחילה הוא דלא:
Rashi on Nedarim 47b:3:1.english: Rava said - Actually, I can tell you that replacements are like that which grows [from the forbidden item] and are forbidden, and therefore ab initio she should not borrow and eat, but after the fact it is well and good. And that which we said earlier in this chapter (Nedarim 43a): "[If] one is prohibited by vow from [deriving] benefit from his fellow and has nothing to eat, he [the fellow] gives [food] to this [third] person, and this one [the prohibited person] comes and takes [it] from this [third] person" — is not comparable to this [case], for [in that case] it is not incumbent upon this [fellow] to support him, and [when] this one gives [food] to that [third] person, one can say he is not giving it to him because of the one prohibited by vow, rather it is a mere gift that he is giving to that other person. However, [regarding] this husband, who stands [obligated] to support her, I might say that it should be forbidden for him to pay the creditor — [therefore Rava says] it is only ab initio that it is not [permitted].

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:4:1.english: Come and hear - that [it is] permitted even ab initio.

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:4:2.hebrew: המקדש בערלה - שהוא איסור הנאה, אינה מקודשת:
Rashi on Nedarim 47b:4:2.english: One who betroths [a woman] with orla - Since it is forbidden for benefit, she is not betrothed.

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:4:3.hebrew: מכרן וקידש בדמיהן מקודשת - אלמא דחליפין לאו כגידולין דמו, דגידולין אסור ובחליפין משתרי:
Rashi on Nedarim 47b:4:3.english: [If] he sold them and betrothed [her] with their money, she is betrothed - Evidently, replacements are not like growths, for growths are forbidden, whereas with replacements it is permitted.

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:4:4.hebrew: ה"נ - מיירי דלכתחילה לא ימכור, ואם קידש בדמיהם, מאי דעבד עבד:
Rashi on Nedarim 47b:4:4.english: Here too - [The Mishnah] refers to [a case] where he may not sell [them] initially, and if he betrothed [a woman] with their proceeds, what he has done is done.

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:5:1.english: I am hereby to you [like] an item dedicated [to the Temple] - My property shall be to you [like] an item dedicated [to the Temple].

Rashi on Nedarim 47b:5:2.english: The one prohibited by the vow is prohibited - But the one who imposed the vow is permitted [to benefit from him].

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:2:1.hebrew: תא שמע האומר לאשתו קונם שאני נהנה לך - ותלה הדבר בתשמיש, שאמר: "הנאת תשמישך עלי אם תיהנה משלי", דאל"כ, כיון דמשועבד לה לא מצי מדיר לה. אי נמי, דאדרה כשהיא ארוסה (או) ונישאת:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:2:1.english: Come and hear: One who says to his wife, "Konam that I benefit from you" - And he made the matter dependent on marital relations, in that he said, "The benefit of your marital relations [is forbidden] to me if you benefit from mine," for if not so, since he is obligated to her [in marital relations], he cannot prohibit her [by a vow]. Alternatively, [it is a case] where he imposed the vow on her while she was betrothed (or) and [then] she was married.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:2:2.hebrew: לוה ובעלי חובין נפרעין - כדאמר: לותה ואכלה ועמדה ומיאנה, אין לה מזונות; הא לא מיאנה, יש לה מזונות. ואפילו לרבנן דחנן דאמרי "הניח מעותיו על קרן הצבי", ה"מ במפרנס אשת חבירו סתם, אבל הלוה לה בתורת הלואה — נפרע מן הבעל. וא"ת: ולרבנן דחנן, היאך פורע חובה, הרי אסור לפרוע למי שמודר הנאה ממנו? וי"ל: דהיינו בפורע חוב חבירו, שהוא יכול לתובעו ולומר "פרע לי מה שפרעתי בשבילך", והוי כאילו הלוהו ממש; אבל באשתו, אינו חייב לפרוע לו כלל מה שפרע בשבילה:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:2:2.english: "She may borrow, and the creditors can collect" - As it is stated [in the Talmud]: [If] she borrowed, ate, and then stood up and performed mi'un [refusal of a minor's marriage], she does not have [a claim for] sustenance; [which implies that if] she did not perform mi'un, she does have [a claim for] sustenance. And even according to the Rabbis [who dispute] Chanan, who say [that one who sustains another's wife] "has placed his money on the horn of a deer" [i.e., lost it] — that applies only to one who sustains his fellow's wife without specification, but [if] one lent to her as a loan, he collects from the husband. And if you say: According to the Rabbis [who dispute] Chanan, how can he [the husband] pay her debt? Behold, it is forbidden to pay [a debt] for one who is prohibited by a vow from benefiting from him! And one can say: That [prohibition] applies to one who pays his fellow's debt, where he can sue him and say, "Pay me what I paid on your behalf," so it is as if he literally lent him [the money]; but in the case of his wife, he [the husband] is not obligated at all to pay him what he paid on her behalf.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:2:3.hebrew: מאי טעמא בעלי חובות חוזרין ונפרעין, לאו דחילופין לאו כגדולין דמו - ושרו ליהנות למודר. דאי אסורין, א"כ מעות שמוסרין לה המלוים הוו חליפי מעות הבעל. ומההוא דתנן (לעיל נדרים דף מג -): "המודר הנאה מחבירו הולך אצל חנוני הרגיל אצלו וכו'", לא מצי למיפשט בעיין, דסתם חנוני לית ליה למיתבע מידי מן המדיר; הילכך מתנת חנם הוא דיהיב לחנוני, ואם ירצה חנוני, עדיין יוכל לתבוע מודר. אבל הכא, דבעלי חובות יש לו על הבעל — שהבעל חייב במזונות אשתו — א"כ מה שהם מלוים לה הוי ממש חליפי מעות הבעל:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:2:3.english: What is the reason the creditors come back and collect? Is it not because replacements are not like that which grows [from the original]? - and they are permitted for the one subject to the vow [mudar] to benefit from. For if they were forbidden, if so, the money that the lenders hand over to her would be replacements for the husband's money. And from that [Mishnah] which we learned (above, Nedarim 43a): "One who is under a vow not to benefit from his fellow goes to the shopkeeper who is accustomed [to deal] with him, etc.," [the Gemara] could not resolve our dilemma, because an ordinary shopkeeper has nothing to claim from the one who imposed the vow [madir]; therefore, it is a free gift that [the madir] gives to the shopkeeper, and if the shopkeeper wishes, he can still claim [payment] from the mudar. But here, where the creditors have [a claim] against the husband — since the husband is obligated in his wife's sustenance — if so, what they lend her is literally replacements for the husband's money.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:3:1.hebrew: דילמא לכתחילה הוא דלא הא דיעבד עבד - כלומר: לותה — דוקא בדיעבד קאמר, דאז בעלי חובין נפרעין, אבל לכתחילה לא תלוה. וכשלותה — הרי זה דיעבד, שאין זה חליפי איסור ממה שעדיין האיסור לא בא. אבל מעיקרא סלקא דעתך דשרו רבנן ללוות בתחילה ולגרום דברים שיבא לידי איסור; לכן פשיט מיניה דחליפי (טומאה) מותרין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:3:1.english: Perhaps it is [the case] that [one should] not ab initio, whereas after the fact it is done - That is to say: [when the baraita states that] "she borrows," it specifically means after the fact, [namely,] that then the creditors collect [from the husband], but ab initio she may not borrow. And once she has borrowed, this is [a case of] after the fact, for this is not [considered] replacements of a forbidden item since the forbidden item has not yet arrived. However, originally it entered your mind [to think] that the Rabbis permitted [her] to borrow ab initio and to cause things that will lead to a forbidden item; therefore, he resolved from it that replacements (of impurity) [i.e., of a forbidden item] are permitted.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:4:1.hebrew: ת"ש המקדש [בערלה] (בדמי ערלה פי' בדמים של ערלה) או כלאי הכרם אינה מקודשת, משום דאיסורי הנאה אינון ולא הוי ממון - מכרם וקדש בדמיהן, בערלה וכלאי הכרם מקודשת, דאינן תופסין דמיהן; אלמא שרי לאיתהנויי בחליפין, דאי אסור ליהנות, היה לנו לומר דאסור לשהות עמה באותם קידושין:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:4:1.english: Come [and] hear: One who betroths [a woman] [with orlah] (with the proceeds of orlah — meaning, with the money of orlah) or [with] kil'ei hakerem [diverse kinds of the vineyard], she is not betrothed, because they are items from which benefit is forbidden and are not [considered] money - [If] he sold them and betrothed [her] with their proceeds, regarding orlah and kil'ei hakerem she is betrothed, for they do not transfer [their prohibition to] their proceeds; thus, it is permitted to benefit from the exchange [of forbidden items], for if it were forbidden to benefit [from them], we would have to say that it is forbidden to remain with her [as husband and wife] through that betrothal.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:4:2.hebrew: ה"נ הא לכתחילה הא דיעבד - כלומר: אכתי איבעיא ליה אי מותר לכתחילה הוא, או דוקא דיעבד אבל לכתחילה לא. ואע"ג דעל ידי הקידושין הוא נהנה ממנה לכתחילה — דוקא בקידושין, שלא תקנו חכמים להפקיע הקידושין, דכיון שהיא אשתו הוא חייב ליהנות ממנה; אבל משאר הנאות, אם אסור למוכרם — אם לקח מן המעות כלי, אסור ליהנות ממנו, דאסור בחלופיהן קרינן ביה. מפירו"ש רבינ"ו שמעו"ן מקוצ"י:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:4:2.english: Here too, this is ab initio, [and] this is ex post facto - That is to say: it is still a question whether it is permitted ab initio, or only ex post facto, but not ab initio. And even though through the betrothal he benefits from her ab initio — [that is] specifically with betrothal, for the Sages did not enact to nullify the betrothal, since once she is his wife, he is obligated to benefit from her; but regarding other benefits, if it is forbidden to sell them — if he bought a vessel with the money, it is forbidden to benefit from it, for we apply to it [the rule of] "forbidden in its replacements." From the commentary of Rabbeinu Shimshon of Coucy:

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:5:1.english: "I am hereby [forbidden] to you [as] cherem" — the one prohibited by the vow is prohibited - For this is what he is saying: "My property is hereby forbidden to you."

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:5:2.hebrew: הרי אתה עלי חרם - הכי קאמר: הרי ממונך עלי כחרם, וחרם הוי הקדש, דסתם חרם לבדק הבית:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:5:2.english: You are hereby [forbidden] to me [like] a cherem - This is what he means: "Your property is hereby [forbidden] to me like a cherem," and a cherem is consecrated property, for an unspecified cherem goes to the upkeep of the Temple.

Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:5:3.hebrew: ומותרים בדברים של עולי בבל כגון בור שבאמצע הדרך שעשאוהו עולי גולה - לפי שהפקירוהו לכל ישראל, ולא נתנוהו להם להיות שותפין (כך) [בו] לענין שיוכל האחד לאסור חלק חבירו:
Tosafot on Nedarim 47b:5:3.english: "And they are permitted [to benefit] from objects belonging to those who ascended from Babylonia," such as a cistern in the middle of the road that those who ascended from the exile made - Because they declared it ownerless for all of Israel, and did not give it to them to be partners in it with respect to one being able to prohibit his fellow's share.
